svg.title: The four NAT behaviours: full cone, address-restricted cone, port-restricted cone and symmetric, from most to least permissive, with a one-line explanation of how each maps and filters traffic
svg.text: Four NAT behaviours, from most to least permissive
mapping decides which external port a client gets, filtering decides who may send back through it
One internal address and port always maps to one external port; any host can send to it.
Same external port for every destination, but only hosts the client has sent to (any port) may reply.
Same external port for every destination, but only the exact host and port the client has sent to may reply.
Peer-to-peer: works when both sides send
A new external port for each destination, and only that destination may reply, so a peer cannot predict the port.
